activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type III Regions

examples.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral 

$$
\displaystyle \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{x}} 2y\: \mathrm{d}y \right ]  \mathrm{d}A,
$$

given that $D$ is the region in the $xz$-plane bounded by the lines $z=0,$ $x= 1$ and the line $z =x.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}2y\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}x\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to calculate this double integral, we plot $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/1d102b63c3deb8121ea88cdc994b9410cf28f9c3bb29abc5ea4a14d7e1e7c389.png)

 

Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}x\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x[z]_{z=0}^{z=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
{∭}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{∗}^{∗}{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx
$$

The triple integral above is defined over the type III region given by

$$
S={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 2x,\,0\le y\le xz}.
$$

What is the value of $a+b?$
feedback.worked_solution:
A type III region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,z)\le y\le {u}_{2}(x,z)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type III region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/0603bed12c6af74e46544d8bebc52362aed95a9a5ad7418ea4faaf228f3b5241.png)

 

If $R$ is a type III region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,z)=0,\,{u}_{2}(x,z)=xz.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.
$$

 

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 2x}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2x}[{\int }_{0}^{xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dz\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=(0)+(2x)=2x.
$$
